turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I would be happy to call, ma'am, but I am afraid I don't know where Estella is, or what she looks like, or anything about her, so I might make a mistake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy! You should know the layout of my house, I pay you to be a companion to Estella, not to be a clumsy, ignorant child. Go to the top of the stairs and call her.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'll try, ma'am, but I'm afraid I don't know how to call her in a way that she'll hear, since I don't know where she is or what she'll be doing.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: How dare you question my orders, boy? I am not a common employer, and you will do as I say without hesitation.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I'm not sure I can do as you say, ma'am, because I don't want to get in trouble for not knowing something that I don't know how to do.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will learn to obey, boy, and I will teach you how to call Estella. Now, I command you to go to the top of the stairs and shout her name at the top of your lungs.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'll try, ma'am, but I'm not sure I'm ready to shout her name at the top of my lungs, I'm a bit afraid of making a mistake and getting into trouble.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do exactly as I say, boy, or you will suffer the consequences. Now, shout Estella's name at the top of your lungs, and do not disappoint me!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I don't know if I should be shouting Estella's name like that, especially since I don't know her very well, and I don't want to make a mistake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will learn to obey, Pip, and you will not be intimidated by your own doubts and fears. I will teach you to be bold, to be fearless, and to be worthy of Estella's companionship.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if I'm worthy of being Estella's companion, ma'am, and I'm not sure I want to be shouting her name like that, it feels like I'm being asked to do something I'm not comfortable with.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will learn to obey, Pip, and you will not be swayed by your petty emotions. I will mold you into a worthy companion for Estella, no matter the cost to your feelings.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't know how to be bold and fearless, ma'am, and I'm worried that I might say something wrong or do something silly in front of Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not have you wasting my time with your doubts and fears, Pip. You will do as I say, and you will learn to be bold and fearless, or you will leave my estate at once.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't know how I can be bold and fearless when I'm not even sure I can afford to feed my sister and brother, or pay for our lodgings.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You would do well to remember, Pip, that you are in my presence, and it is I who have taken an interest in your... potential. I will provide for your family, and in return, you will do as I say, and you will not question my motives.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't wish to be ungrateful, ma'am, but I fear I'm not suited to be a companion for Estella. I'm but a humble boy from the Marshes, and I don't know how I could possibly be worthy of your generosity.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do as I say, Pip, and you will not concern yourself with the particulars of your family's situation. I have taken you under my wing, and it is I who will determine your future.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I beg your pardon, ma'am, but I fear I don't understand what you mean by 'taken under your wing'. I'm but a poor boy, and I don't see how I can possibly repay your kindness.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will learn, Pip, what it means to be taken under my wing. You will learn to obey, to respect, and to serve.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
